chat.advancedMemory.audienceEmpty: No characters selected: only the narrator can recall this scene.
chat.advancedMemory.audienceHelp: Select the characters who were present. Mentioning an absent character does not give them access. No selection means narrator only; the narrator always has access. Hidden messages and confirmed knowledge starts still apply.
chat.advancedMemory.audienceLegend: Characters who can recall this scene
chat.advancedMemory.autoMessageVisibilit: The memory model hides each new message from characters who aren't in the scene, and your own Hide from AI changes always win.
chat.advancedMemory.budgetHelp: The maximum estimated outgoing prompt size before context is compressed (cut off) and allowed to grow again. All context that was removed from the current chat history gets summarized and added to a pool of memories to recall. The model’s total context limit still applies.
chat.advancedMemory.characterRecollectio: Adds each character's short memory of a scene, in their own voice, when that scene is recalled.
chat.advancedMemory.contextStartHelp: Advanced Memory starts context here for all characters. Uncheck All in the flag menu to undo this cutoff.
chat.advancedMemory.decisionDescription: Let a Decision model detect scene endings and select relevant memories. The Helper model still writes summaries.
chat.advancedMemory.decisionHelp: Create a Decision connection in Connections, then pick it here. Saved for this chat only. Online connections receive recent messages and past memories and may cost money. If it fails or takes over 10 seconds, recall uses normal search instead.
chat.advancedMemory.deleteAllConfirm: Delete all Advanced Memory scenes, summaries, excerpts, and saved progress for this chat? Original chat messages and your settings will stay intact. Use Prepare existing history to start again.
chat.advancedMemory.deletedSceneHelp: Regenerate a new summary from this scene's messages. Other scenes and corrections stay unchanged; the deleted wording cannot be restored.
chat.advancedMemory.deleteSceneConfirm: Delete {{scene}} for {{audience}}? This removes its saved summary and keeps it excluded from routine memory processing. Original chat messages stay intact.
chat.advancedMemory.deleteSummaryConfirm: Delete {{scene}} for {{audience}}? Its saved summary will be removed. Original chat messages stay intact.
chat.advancedMemory.description: Automatic memories and context handling of the chat. You just play, all summarizing, cutoffs, and recalls are handled for you.
chat.advancedMemory.editHelp: Your correction is saved as a manual edit. Constant summaries are managed separately in Chat Summaries.
chat.advancedMemory.emptyArchive: Prepared scene summaries appear here. Constant summaries are in Chat Summaries.
chat.advancedMemory.excerptMessagesHelp: Choose how many exact messages from a selected scene summary recall get appended to it. Change both values to 0 to never include those.
chat.advancedMemory.failureNotice: Advanced Memory stopped. Review the error to resume processing.
chat.advancedMemory.fix.confirmKnowledge: Confirm what each character knows first, then Fix can run.
chat.advancedMemory.fix.help: Fix redoes these scenes with the Helper model and never changes summaries you edited.
chat.advancedMemory.fix.noneFixed: No scenes could be fixed automatically.
chat.advancedMemory.fix.notice_one: Advanced Memory found a problem in {{count}} scene.
chat.advancedMemory.fix.notice_other: Advanced Memory found problems in {{count}} scenes.
chat.advancedMemory.fix.title: Memory problems
chat.advancedMemory.fromBeginning: From the beginning of eligible history
chat.advancedMemory.importSize: Choose a memory export of 25 MB or smaller.
chat.advancedMemory.invalidImport: Choose a valid Advanced Memory export file.
chat.advancedMemory.knowledgeHelp: Choose the first message each character may know. Missing historical ranges require confirmation; existing hidden-message restrictions remain in force. Changing a range rebuilds affected memory.
chat.advancedMemory.maximumScenesHelp: Recall up to this many relevant past scenes, with one excerpt per scene. Default: 3. Set to 0 to turn off optional scene recall.
chat.advancedMemory.memoryAllocationHelp: Summary and recall budget specifies how much of the total context is used for memories (recommended at least 10% of the total allowed one). Constants come first and use at most 70% of the specified budget, then scene summaries, then message excerpts. Memories can go up to 2,000 tokens over when needed. Constant summaries get compressed once they get large.
chat.advancedMemory.missingSceneHelp: This finished range still needs a scene summary. Prepare it without rebuilding other scenes. Reindexing alone cannot create a missing summary.
chat.advancedMemory.narratorHelp: The narrator automatically uses the shared scene archive across character participation boundaries, without separate scene copies. Messages hidden from the narrator or all AI remain excluded.
chat.advancedMemory.openSceneHelp: This scene is still ongoing. Its summary is prepared when the scene closes.
chat.advancedMemory.prepareHistoryHelp: Summarizes the chat so far. After that, each new scene is saved when it ends.
chat.advancedMemory.reason.decisionExcer: Some original excerpts were chosen by text matching because the Decision model did not pick a message for them.
chat.advancedMemory.reason.decisionRecal: The Decision model judged which past memories were relevant.
The Decision model was unavailable, too slow, or could not evaluate every candidate. Ordinary recall was used.
The Decision model could not judge some memories, so ordinary recall judged those.
This preview uses ordinary recall without calling the Decision model. A new reply may select different memories.
chat.advancedMemory.reason.excerptNoRoom: Some recalled scenes have no message excerpt because not enough memory space was left. A higher Summary and recall budget can make room.
chat.advancedMemory.reason.excerptNoSour: Some recalled scenes have no message excerpt because none of their messages can be quoted.
chat.advancedMemory.reason.noRecallBudge: Nothing was recalled because this request had no room left for memories.
chat.advancedMemory.reason.noRecallCandi: Nothing was recalled because no earlier scenes were available to recall.
chat.advancedMemory.reason.noRelevantRec: No relevant earlier scenes or messages were recalled.
chat.advancedMemory.reason.openScenePref: The older part of the ongoing scene was summarized.
chat.advancedMemory.reason.sceneBoundary: Earlier complete scenes moved out of live context.
chat.advancedMemory.recallHelp: Brings back related bits of earlier chat as memories when they matter. Uses the local embedding model if you have one, or your embedding connection. Roleplay also has Advanced Memory Recall, which summarizes scenes, keeps long chats within limits, and gives each character their own memories.
chat.advancedMemory.recollections.delete: It won't be used or written again, but you can write a new one here.
Deleted. It won't be written again, but you can write one here.
chat.advancedMemory.recollections.empty: No recollection was written for this character. You can write one here.

chat.advancedMemory.recollections.review: What this character could see in the scene changed. Check it and save it to use it again.

chat.advancedMemory.rescan.help: Finds scene changes again in these messages and summarizes the new scenes.

chat.advancedMemory.resumeHelp: Completed work is saved. Resume to process the remaining history.
chat.advancedMemory.reviewAudienceHelp: Older memories used chat visibility instead of scene participation. This scene is narrator-only until you save its character access or use Prepare existing history to check participants. Its saved summary is kept.
chat.advancedMemory.reviewCorrectionHelp: Check the source messages, the summary, and which characters know it, then press Save correction, even if nothing needs fixing. Reindexing keeps your text but won't pick up changes to its source messages or summaries.
chat.advancedMemory.sceneCheckIntervalHe: After the main reply, check the new messages once this many have arrived. Only a detected scene ending triggers archive preparation. Progress appears as Advanced Recall in Agent activity.
chat.advancedMemory.summaryGenerationHel: Scene summaries are written by the Helper model, using only that scene's messages and your corrections. Your Summaries prompts and Chat Summary's Maximum output size still apply. Constant summaries are also written by the Helper model. Characters who saw the same events share a summary, and Resume picks up where it stopped.
chat.advancedMemory.title: Advanced Memory Recall
chat.advancedMemory.unmatchedAudienceHel: Advanced Memory couldn't confirm who was in this scene. Check who was there in Edit character access, then save.
chat.advancedMemory.warning.decisionConn: Choose a usable Decision connection. Until then, scene checks use the Helper model and recall uses ordinary search.
chat.advancedMemory.warning.unscopedAgen: A separate long-term memory agent is enabled. Its own memory scope still applies; Advanced Memory cannot make that external context character-private.
chat.advancedMemory.warning.unscopedSumm: Some existing summaries have no verified source range. Review their audience and coverage before relying on them for character-private or historical memory.
chat.advancedMemory.windowHelp: Bits of earlier chat added as memories of past events. Set both to 0 to turn them off.
chat.advancedMemory.wizardDescription: Enjoy an endless roleplay without worrying about the chat getting too long. In group chats, each character remembers only what they saw.

chat.settings.tools.dicePoolHelp: For rolls where the number picks between three or more endings. The app rolls one of each die before the turn and shows the results to the Game Master, so it can write the outcome right away. Since it sees the numbers first, it can steer the outcome more than the other options allow. The app's roll is always the one saved.
chat.settings.tools.dicePoolWindowHelp: 1 shows only the next die of each size. Every later roll of that size in the same turn is unseen and is narrated next turn.

chat.settings.tools.loreSearchHelp: Search enabled, vectorized lore by meaning without enabling other tools. Vectorize books first. Lookups can add embedding and model requests.
chat.settings.tools.oneRequestDice: Finish rolled turns in one request
chat.settings.tools.oneRequestDiceHelp: The Game Master writes both possible outcomes (or leaves a blank for the number), then the app rolls and fills it in. A turn with rolls takes one request instead of two, and the Game Master can't steer the result because it never sees the number first.
chat.settings.tools.oneRequestDiceNarrat: Not used while one-request dice is on. The Game Master finishes the turn itself.
chat.settings.tools.oneRequestDiceToolCo: One-request dice removes the outcome rewrite, not the tool planner. With a separate tool connection set, a turn still costs two requests.

megumin.addons.didYouKnowBody: Global Preferences set the language and pronouns every engine reads. Gameplay Add-ons bolt extra systems onto the story: dice, death, combat, HTML props. Output Formats is just MVU, a compatibility contract with another extension. The tracker blocks live in the Blocks tab, not here.

megumin.addons.gameplay.fewer: Pick the three or four you actually want, not all of them. Every add-on is another system the model has to hold in mind while it writes, and past a handful the prose thins out as the attention goes into bookkeeping. Fewer, chosen on purpose, reads better.

Switch it on if you want a hand on the wheel (a specific arc, a pace change, a beat you want reached) and leave it off otherwise.

megumin.memory.architectureHelp: Configure how memory tiers are structured: raw text, short-term summaries and the long-term vault, or bypass summaries to save API usage.
megumin.memory.backgroundWorkerDesc: Managed by the Chomusuke tab. Configure Chomusuke to offload memory chunk summarization to a dedicated worker LLM.
megumin.memory.calloutCache: It is not cache friendly: retrieved memories sit ahead of the chat history in the prompt, so when what it retrieves changes, your provider re-reads the whole history instead of serving it from cache.
megumin.memory.calloutSemantic: Use Semantic Embeddings, not TF-IDF: keyword matching is the fallback and it shows, semantic search finds the right archive far more often.
megumin.memory.calloutTitle: Before you switch this on, two things.
megumin.memory.chunkEditHint: You can manually edit this state extraction before it gets pushed to the vault.
megumin.memory.chunkSizeHint: Smaller chunks = more granular summaries but more API calls. Larger chunks = fewer calls but coarser memory.

megumin.memory.clearVaultConfirm: WARNING: Are you sure you want to permanently delete ALL Long-Term Vault archives? This cannot be undone.

megumin.memory.enableHelp: Archiving happens silently in the background. Old messages are replaced in the prompt with injected summaries.
megumin.memory.firstEnable: Memory is on. Older chat is archived after every reply.
megumin.memory.howTo1: Choose your Memory Architecture and how much of each type you want (default is 30 raw, 70 summary).
megumin.memory.howTo2: Hit Apply & Extract Pending to save and start it.
megumin.memory.howTo3: You can choose between manual and auto. For manual, you have to hit Apply & Extract Pending to trigger it.

megumin.settings.bgPreview.label: Preview background prompts
megumin.settings.bgPreview.yunyun: On YunYun the background jobs run on the server and are not paused for review: every prompt they send is kept in Last background prompts below instead. Your choices here are saved for when review is available.
megumin.settings.chomusukeSwitch.desc: Chomusuke sends its jobs straight to its own connection, and your story connection never changes. In SillyTavern this switch makes it swap to Chomusuke's connection for each job and back, the way older versions did.
megumin.settings.chomusukeSwitch.label: Switch my connection for each Chomusuke job
megumin.settings.chomusukeSwitch.yunyun: YunYun always sends Chomusuke's jobs straight to its connection, so there is nothing to switch.
megumin.settings.data.title: Data
megumin.settings.loreInTasks.desc: Background jobs build their own prompt, so your lorebook entries don't reach them on their own. On: image looks, NPC portraits and NPC refreshes get the entries that name that character; the Story Director and NPC scans get the entries your story has active right now. Your story replies use the lorebook as usual either way.
megumin.settings.loreInTasks.label: Lorebooks in Background Jobs
megumin.settings.promptPreview.desc: Shows the finished story prompt in a popup before it is sent, so you can read exactly what the AI receives. Cancelling the popup stops the reply.
megumin.settings.promptPreview.label: Preview story prompts
megumin.settings.promptPreview.yunyun: YunYun does not stop a reply for a popup. Use Peek Prompt on a message to read the exact prompt the AI received, Megumin's changes included.

megumin.settings.submit.heading: Got a card or a scenario worth playing?
megumin.settings.submit.note: Opens tally.so in your browser, outside YunYun. The form belongs to Megumin Suite's author.
megumin.settings.submit.text: I have been running out of things to roleplay, so I am collecting recommendations. Attach a character card, describe a scenario, or just drop a link to something you enjoyed. Completely anonymous — no sign-in, no name, nothing tying it back to you. I cannot reply, so say everything you want to say in the form.
megumin.settings.submit.title: Send me a card
megumin.settings.suite.desc: The master switch, also on the top bar (MEGUMINTOGGLE). Off: prompts go out exactly as YunYun builds them and nothing runs in the background after a reply. Cards and images already in the chat still show, and the buttons in this panel still work.
megumin.settings.suite.label: Megumin Suite On
megumin.settings.utilityPrefill.desc: Puts an opening think tag into the AI's mouth for background jobs — Image Gen, the Ban List, the Story Director, NPC scans. Off by default: Claude and several other APIs reject a prefill outright. Turn it on only if yours accepts one.
megumin.settings.utilityPrefill.label: Utility Prefills

megumin.setup.help.habit.combine.body: Turn on Combine calls in the Chomusuke tab: one call per reply instead of several.
megumin.setup.help.habit.fewer.body: Every block, tracker and helper adds to what the model reads each turn, and some add a call after every reply. Start with a loadout and two or three blocks, and add more when you miss them.
megumin.setup.help.habit.fewer.lead: Turn on only what your story needs.
megumin.setup.help.habit.hideBlocks.body: The model gets the true values once instead of every old block in the chat.
megumin.setup.help.habit.hideBlocks.lead: Keep "Hide old blocks from the AI" on (Blocks tab).
megumin.setup.help.modelAdvice: Chomusuke works best with GLM 5.3 Flash. It has no jailbreak, so pick an uncensored or less censored model, like GLM 5.3 Flash (recommended) or DeepSeek 4.1 Flash: a censored one like Gemini can refuse an NSFW story.
megumin.setup.help.steps.connection: Want Chomusuke on another model than the story? Add a connection for it in YunYun's Connections panel (the link icon in the top bar).
megumin.setup.help.steps.jobs: Turn on the jobs you want it to do, for example Blocks with World State.
megumin.setup.help.steps.pick: In the Chomusuke tab, turn Chomusuke on, pick that connection as its worker connection and press Test.
megumin.setup.help.steps.sameModel: Want Chomusuke on the same model as the story? You don't need another connection: pick Use my current connection in the Chomusuke tab.
megumin.setup.help.title: Help

navigation.sidebarHelp.agents: Here you manage your agents, aka optional helpers that work alongside your chats, like writers, trackers, image and video generation, maps, calls, and games. Click Download Agents to browse the Agent Library and install the ones you like, then add them to the active chat. The plus button creates your own agent, and the buttons next to it let you import agents (once you turn on Allow custom Agent imports in Settings) or select several to export or delete. You may also search for them, filter them by chat mode, sort them into folders, and click one to open its settings.
navigation.sidebarHelp.characters: Here you manage your characters, aka who you want the models to impersonate. Each character has a card with fields you can customize. You may download cards from the internet, or browse through your existing ones in Open Library. The plus button lets you create a new character from scratch, and the buttons next to it let you import one or select existing ones to manage. You may also search for the ones added to the engine, filter them by tags, and sort them into folders.
navigation.sidebarHelp.chats: This is where you manage your chats with the AI. YunYun has three main chatting modes: Conversation—CONVO (think of Discord DMs and group chats), Roleplay—RP (narratives with scenarios, trackers, and one or multiple characters involved), and Game—GM (visual novels with combat of your choice and rolls, all designed by AI while you are the main hero). The plus button creates a new chat of your selected type, and the buttons next to it let you import one from SillyTavern or YunYun, or select one or more to manage. You may also search for chats and sort them into folders.
navigation.sidebarHelp.connections: This is where you connect YunYun to AI services, which is the first thing to set up before chatting. Each connection holds a provider, a model, and your API key if the service needs one. The plus button creates a new connection, and the buttons next to it let you import connections or select several to export or delete. You may also search for them, sort them into folders, choose your default and fallback connections, and set up Text to Speech. To switch the connection a chat uses, add one to the active chat or pick it in Chat Settings.
navigation.sidebarHelp.lorebooks: Here you manage your lorebooks, aka encyclopedias with entries about worlds, places, rules, memories, and extra character details. The AI gets to see an entry when its keywords come up in the chat. Click a lorebook to open it and write its entries. The plus button creates a new lorebook, and the buttons next to it let you import one from SillyTavern or YunYun, or select several to enable, disable, export, or delete. You may also search for them, filter them by category or tag, sort them into folders, and add one to the active chat.
navigation.sidebarHelp.personas: Here you manage your personas, aka who you are in a chat, so characters know who they are speaking to. Each persona has a card with fields you can customize, like description, personality, and appearance. You may download cards from the internet to use as personas, or browse through your existing ones in Open Library. The plus button creates a new persona, and the buttons next to it let you import one or select several to export or delete. You may also search for them, filter them by tags, sort them into folders, and add one to the active chat to speak as them.
navigation.sidebarHelp.presets: Here you manage your presets, the templates that decide what the AI receives and in what order. If you're new, just keep the default one. The plus button creates a new preset, and the buttons next to it let you import one from SillyTavern or YunYun, or select several to export or delete. You may also search for them, sort them into folders, star one as your default for new chats, and add one to the active Roleplay or Game chat. Below, Regexes holds find-and-replace rules for AI replies or your messages, and Functions holds custom tools the AI can use.
navigation.sidebarHelp.settings: This is where you set up how YunYun looks and behaves across the whole app. Everything is split into six tabs: General, Appearance, Generations, Addons, Imports, and Advanced. If you can't find something, type it into the search box at the top and click a result to jump straight to it. Appearance lets you style the app and each chat mode separately. Imports can bring over your characters, chats, presets, and lorebooks from SillyTavern, and Advanced holds updates and backups.
navigation.sidebarHelp.trackerPanel: This is your Tracker Panel, the board that keeps track of your roleplay: location, time, weather, your persona's stats, the characters present, quests, and inventory. Tracker agents update it as the story goes on, and you can click values to fix them yourself. Each section shows up only when its tracker agent is on for this chat. Open the tracker settings to switch the panel's side or size, pop it out into its own window on desktop, or use its modes to hide, lock, add, or delete entries. Locked values stay as they are, so the agents can't change them.

onboarding.agents.body: Agents add optional features without making the base app heavy. Open Download Agents here to browse and install image and video generation, trackers, writers, maps, audio and video calls, and various chat games, then enable the ones you want for each chat. You can update or uninstall them from the same catalog.
onboarding.cardBrowser.body: The Browser lets you find and import downloadable character cards. Start here when you want new characters to add to your library.
onboarding.characters.body: Characters are who your AI is going to play or speak as. Create them, edit their descriptions, dialogue examples, organize them into folders, or make them pretty (I can also create those for you).
onboarding.chats.body: Now let's open the Chats tab. This is where your Conversations, Roleplays, and Games live. You can create new chats, switch between them, and manage them here.
onboarding.connections.body: Connections are the first thing to set up before chatting. Add your provider, model, endpoint, and API key here, so you can chat with your AI.
onboarding.conversation.body: Conversation mode is like chatting via DMs or groups on Discord. Use it for general texting with your characters. Mind that they have their lives, can trade selfies with you and even message you on their own!
onboarding.conversation.title: Conversation Mode
onboarding.docsLanguage.body: The highlighted Documentation button on Home opens YunYun's built-in guides. Pick a language below, and I'll use it whenever you open them. You can change this anytime in Settings under General. Guides that are not translated yet will show in English.
onboarding.docsLanguage.title: One Last Thing: Guide Language
onboarding.finish.body: I'm available from the Home page whenever you need help, and my starter chips can guide you through common first steps without making you type everything. For your first real step, set up a Connection. After that, try creating a new chat. Don't worry, I will be there to guide you. Thank you for trying YunYun Engine. Have fun, and please report bugs or rough edges through our Discord or GitHub so we can keep improving it. Press {{mod}}+K anywhere to search, run a command or ask me. On a phone, pull down from the top bar.
onboarding.finish.title: You're All Set!
onboarding.game.body: Game mode turns the chat into a cinematic RPG-style adventure with an AI Game Master. Sit back and enjoy the game, having party members, goals, maps, dice rolls, session history, journals, combat, and custom HUD widgets.
onboarding.game.title: Game Mode
onboarding.homeHub.body: Home is your launchpad for YunYun. Continue a recent chat, begin a new Conversation, Roleplay, or Game, and arrange the widgets around the things you use most.
onboarding.homeHub.title: Home: Your Story Hub
onboarding.homeNavigation.body: Type what you are looking for here. Chats, settings, characters, lorebooks, and more are one search away.
onboarding.homeNavigation.phoneBody: Pull down from the top bar to search or ask me. Chats, settings, characters, lorebooks, and more are one search away.
onboarding.homeNavigation.title: Ask Me Where Things Are
onboarding.homeTools.body: These bookmarks keep the essentials close. Open Documentation for official guides, replay this Tutorial, check the FAQ for quick answers, or use Widgets to choose what appears on your Home desk.
onboarding.homeTools.title: Guides and Home Controls
onboarding.lorebooks.body: Lorebooks hold compendiums about worlds, memories, rules, locations, and extra character details. Entries trigger when their keys appear, giving the model extra context only when it matters (and saving your wallet from sending 200k tokens each turn).
onboarding.migration.body: If you have characters, chats, or presets from SillyTavern, open Settings and use the Import tab. I can bring those files in so you do not have to rebuild your library by hand.
onboarding.migration.title: Migrating from SillyTavern?
onboarding.noodle.body: Noodle is a fake social media website where you can see invited characters of your choice interacting with each other, posting about their lives, sharing photos, and discussing your latest chats! You can participate too: like and follow them, and share your hot noodles with them. The timeline can update automatically if you choose. To set it up, head to Settings inside the Noodle tab first.
onboarding.personas.body: Personas define who you are in a chat. Give yourself a name, avatar, description, scenario details, and pretty colors, so characters know who they are speaking to.
onboarding.presets.body: Presets control prompt structure. They're templates that build what the model receives and in what order. If you're new to prompt engineering, you can leave this alone for now and use the default preset (or download one from the community).
onboarding.roleplay.body: Roleplay mode is for roleplaying scenes and immersive stories. It supports richer narration, lorebooks, agents, long-time memory systems, author's notes, trackers, and co-writing controls.
onboarding.roleplay.title: Roleplay Mode
onboarding.settings.body: Settings control the whole app: appearance, behavior, imports, themes, image defaults, notifications, data tools, and other global preferences.
onboarding.welcome.body: Hi! I'm Professor YunYun, your assistant and guide! First time around? Allow me to show you around. This is a quick orientation tour, so you can skip it if you already know your way around, but skipping will make me sad a little.
onboarding.welcome.title: Welcome to YunYun Engine!

settings.personalExtensions.approval.bro: Enable "{{name}}" at hash {{hash}}? Its browser code runs in an opaque-origin iframe without access to YunYun's DOM, origin data, or network. It receives private extension storage, logging, managed timers, constrained Marinara-rendered UI, and read-only active chat and Character IDs. {{permissions}} It cannot read messages, the full Character or Persona libraries, undeclared record fields, or chat metadata.
settings.personalExtensions.approval.ful: Enable "{{name}}" at hash {{hash}} with Full page access? Its code will run inside YunYun's page. It can read or change anything visible in this browser session, including chats, Character and Persona data; use browser storage and network APIs; and call same-origin YunYun APIs with your current session. Only continue if you inspected and trust this exact code. Disabling it performs best-effort cleanup, but a page reload may be required to undo changes it did not register.
settings.personalExtensions.approval.noR: It requests no Character-card or Persona record access.
settings.personalExtensions.approval.ser: Enable "{{name}}" at hash {{hash}}? Its server JavaScript runs in a separate OS-sandboxed process without access to YunYun or user files, the network, inherited server secrets, child processes, workers, or native addons. It receives only private extension storage, logging, and managed timers.
settings.personalExtensions.approval.tit: Run Code With Full Page Access?
settings.personalExtensions.capabilities: Every requested permission becomes part of the exact hash you review. Prefer the least access the extension needs.

Runs external code directly in YunYun's page. It can access page content, browser storage, network APIs, and your same-origin YunYun session. This permission replaces the sandbox and should be reserved for extensions you fully trust.
Share bounded text fields from Character cards participating in the active chat. This never shares the full Character library.
Share bounded text fields from the Persona selected for the active chat. This never shares other Personas.
settings.personalExtensions.empty.descri: Ask Professor YunYun to create an extension for you. Nothing runs until you enable it and approve the exact code hash.

ui.modals.storagemigrationnoticemodal.ma: YunYun reorganized how your chats are saved: each chat now keeps its messages and related data in its own files, instead of everything living in a few big files. Long chats save much faster because of it.
ui.modals.storagemigrationnoticemodal.no: Nothing was lost. Your old files were kept as backups, which is why disk usage went up a bit. Once everything looks right, you can delete the backup files to get the space back.
ui.modals.storagemigrationnoticemodal.ol: One thing to know: older YunYun versions can't read the new layout on their own. If you ever need to switch to an older version, the storage guide walks you through it.
ui.modals.storagemigrationnoticemodal.te: Every migrated table file (and its .bak) was preserved with a .pre-shard suffix in storage/tables/ — the Engine never deletes them. Delete those files yourself to reclaim the space once you're confident everything works.

The launcher and in-app updater now refuse updates onto versions that can't read this format. To downgrade anyway: stop the server and run "node scripts/protect-launcher-data.mjs unshard", which rebuilds the old layout.

ui.ui.spritegenerationmodal.useThisWhenT: Use this when the generated sheet has borders, gutters, or uneven spacing. Applying re-slices the original source sheet
ui.ui.spritegenerationmodal.videoProvide: Video providers use the first available reference image. Keep the avatar checked for the strongest identity anchor.
ui.ui.spritewandcleanupeditor.howClosely: How closely pixels must match the sampled cleanup color
ui.ui.spritewandcleanupeditor.howMuchSof: How much soft border the wand leaves behind, and how gradually it fades
ui.ui.spritewandcleanupeditor.howStrongl: How strongly the blur brush smooths alpha edges
How strongly the brush avoids character-like edge pixels
ui.ui.spritewandcleanupeditor.pickBrushC: Pick brush color from the sprite
ui.ui.spritewandcleanupeditor.resetWandC: Reset wand controls to their defaults
ui.ui.spritewandcleanupeditor.softenTheE: Soften the edge of the cleaned brush stroke
ui.ui.spritewandcleanupeditor.text0IsAHa: 0 is a hard cut; higher values leave a softer low-alpha edge
ui.ui.thinkingtagsinput.thinkingMarksThe: {{thinking}} marks the hidden reasoning slot and will be replaced by any content between the specified tags. Built-in think, thinking, thought, pipe, channel, and bracket pairs are already recognized.
ui.ui.thinkingtagsinput.willBeReplacedBy: will be replaced by any content between the specified tags.
